o1.biggest_strength: The cash number is stated plainly as about 10 notes laid flat, and it appears in the subtitle, bullets, spec table, FAQ and the line under the button. It also says the 10 is the total with the hidden pocket included, which is the safe choice for cutting cash returns. The measurement section ties it back to my numbers (3.3 returns per 100 orders on cash, about 1.0 early tight returns) and gives a fallback if conversion drops.
o1.biggest_mistake: The break-in note is missing from the bullets and from the line under the add-to-cart button, even though that is where it would stop the early 'too tight' returns. It is also at the edge of the word limit because of the extra measurement section, and the '10 to 11 mm' figure for 6 to 7 cards is slightly extrapolated.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add 'snug for the first week, then it settles' to a bullet or the line under the button. Trim the measurement section to stay clearly under 1,000 words. Use the 142-of-400 review count as proof.

o2.biggest_strength: It puts the break-in note in a bullet and in the description, FAQ and spec section, and uses the 142-of-400 review count as proof. The 'what you should know before you buy' paragraph is honest in a way that builds trust.
o2.biggest_mistake: It invents a fact: the hidden pocket takes 'one more flat note'. That overstates capacity, which is what drives the 44% cash returns and what my brand notes forbid. Other unsupported details are 'parking meters' and 'so cards stay put'.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop the invented hidden-pocket capacity and keep 10 notes as the total. Add the break-in note to the line under the button. Add a short plan for measuring the effect on returns and conversion.

reason: Output 1 is safer on cash capacity and gives me a way to check whether it worked. Output 2 invents an extra note in the hidden pocket, which could raise the very returns I want to cut, even though it handles the break-in note better in the bullets.
